recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-31401 unless a later work-group decision changes _count paging semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-31401 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core search clarification for R5. It asked to clarify that _count constrains resources returned in one page rather than the whole search result set, and to add that servers supporting search or history SHALL support checking the _count parameter.
initial_application: The requested wording was implemented before this reconciliation by commit a1cf2cf018130744adb32d8d92f03de8e16f1a93 and merged through PR #1282 in commit 45fd6e3a26c18696dea824fb0470f2e1f60701e0. That patch changed the older 'Servers SHALL NOT return more resources than requested' sentence in source/search.html to the per-page wording and added the search/history _count note.
additional_context: The current Limiting Page Size (_count) section in source/search.html still contains the requested clarification, with later markup/capitalization and adjacent Search Page Count refinements. FHIR-32017 is a same-section follow-up about entry.search.mode and is already represented on the combined branch by commit 7b081822e4e6edcaeea1034ba108efd5b57978a4, so it was not republished here. FHIR-I WGM minutes reference the FHIR-31401 motion, and focused Zulip searches found no direct FHIR-31401 discussion or conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current authoritative FHIR-core search source already conveys the requested per-page _count rule and the required support for checking _count on search/history servers.
